indicator_set: I1 admissible language server exists; I2 selected server states diagnostics + code completion + go-to-definition; I3 selected server states hover type/signature + find-references + rename/refactoring; I4 admissible editor extension in a widely used editor's official marketplace; I5 first-party syntax grammar or editor mode in an official repository of the official_project_set (NOT widened by the admissibility test); I6 admissible dedicated IDE or IDE plugin with a published release dated within 24 months before the evidence cutoff.
scoring_procedure_applied: Count satisfied indicators among I1-I6. 6 -> 100; 5 -> 80; 4 -> 60; 3 -> 40; 2 -> 20; 0 or 1 -> 0. No interpolation, no partial credit, every conjunct of a conjunctive indicator required.

evidence_window.cutoff_handling: Where an artefact's newest release post-dates the cutoff (rust-analyzer's marketplace build of 2026-09-18), the I6 evidence cites an earlier release on or before 2026-09-17.

evidence_collection_order_applied: Python, C++, Rust, Go, Java, TypeScript, Kotlin, Swift, Zig, Quidra (global_rules.evidence_collection_order). Quidra was examined last; every reading recorded under frozen_interpretations_fixed_before_quidra was written down before any Quidra artefact was inspected.

frozen_interpretations_fixed_before_quid.R1_capability_is_stated: For I2 and I3 a capability counts as STATED only when the selected server's published documentation, repository or marketplace listing contains an item that names that capability, or names it in standard alternative wording ('jump-to-definition', 'Find Definitions' = go-to-definition; 'Javadoc hovers' = hover; 'Rename refactoring'/'Rename Symbol' = rename). A generic umbrella term alone ('Code navigation', 'language features', 'IntelliSense') does not state a specific capability. Where the primary feature list was incomplete, the same secondary sources were searched for every language: the server's other published documentation pages, its repository CHANGELOG, and the marketplace long description. This produced 'Go to definition' for Java from the jdt.ls CHANGELOG and produced nothing for Swift's hover; both searches were identical in kind.
frozen_interpretations_fixed_before_quid.R2_I5_publication_test: I5's operative test is 'is published in an official repository of the official_project_set', and global_rules.first_party_definition defines 'first-party' as membership of that set. Publication location is therefore the test, and an artefact vendored from a third party but published and maintained in an official repository counts (this admitted Oracle's java.tmLanguage.json and Kotlin's tree-sitter-kotlin.wasm). The artefact must still be one of the three enumerated forms and must be for the language itself: a TextMate grammar for a manifest format (go.mod, go.sum) is not a grammar for the language, and an EBNF specification of the syntax is not an editor grammar or mode.
frozen_interpretations_fixed_before_quid.R3_clause_c_task_scoping: Clause (c) is read exactly as the Tooling rubric's frozen scoping rule read it: the tool must perform the indicator's named task on source of the language being scored. This is what admits ruff (and hence the Ruff Language Server and the Ruff editor extension) for Python.
frozen_interpretations_fixed_before_quid.R4_IDE_plugin_for_I6: A published extension for a widely used editor that its own language's documentation or vendor treats as an IDE integration counts as an 'IDE plugin' for I6. Applied identically to all ten; no language's I6 turned on whether VS Code is called an IDE, because every language that satisfied I6 also had a second route (a dedicated IDE, or an IntelliJ-family plugin).

admissibility_notes.test_applied: global_rules.tool_admissibility_test, three clauses, for I1, I4, I6 and for selecting the server that I2 and I3 are scored against. I5 keeps the official_project_set test and was not widened.
admissibility_notes.rubric_declared_admission: The frozen metric's own 'admissibility' field states, as part of the rubric text, that the test admits 'jdt.ls for Java, the clangd-based and MSVC-based integrations for C++ and the Pyright/Pylance-class servers for Python'. Independent clause (a)/(b)/(c) evidence was searched for and NOT found for jdt.ls (Eclipse is not in Java's official_project_set; openjdk.org and docs.oracle.com do not name it; openjdk/jdk's CI does not invoke it) nor for Pyright/Pylance (Microsoft is not in Python's official_project_set and maintains neither CPython nor PyPy; docs.python.org contains zero occurrences of 'language server'; the PEPs name Pyright only as a type checker; python/cpython's CI does not invoke it). Because global_rules.prohibited_at_scoring_time forbids reinterpreting the frozen document at scoring time, and because spec section 7 forbids discounting an established language's real editor ecosystem, these two tools were admitted on the rubric's own declaration, recorded per language as admissibility_clause 'rubric-declared'. clangd needed no such help (clause a, LLVM Project).
admissibility_notes.effect_if_the_declaration_were_ignored: Under a strict three-clause-only reading, Java would lose I2 and I3 (its selected server would become Oracle's, whose published feature list names only refactorings) and would score 60 instead of 100; Python would lose I2, I3 and the Pylance route to I4 -- I4 would survive on the Ruff extension via clause (c) -- and would score 60 instead of 80. No other language's score changes. Both alternative figures are stated here so an auditor can recompute either way.

criteria_satisfied: I1 SATISFIED. `quidra lsp` is a Language Server Protocol implementation published by quidra-lang, the sole member of Quidra's official_project_set. Admissibility clause (a).
criteria_failed: I2 NOT SATISFIED. The server's own initialize response advertises only textDocumentSync and documentFormattingProvider, and the only request handlers present are didOpen/didChange/didClose/didSave, textDocument/formatting and the publishDiagnostics notification. Diagnostics are provided; code completion and go-to-definition are not. A conjunctive indicator requires every conjunct (global_rules.indicator_model.no_partial_credit).

The official repository publishes docs/spec/grammar.ebnf, which is an EBNF specification of the language's syntax, not a TextMate grammar, a tree-sitter grammar or an editor major mode. A full file search of the checkout and of the public repository root found no .tmLanguage, .el, .vim, .sublime-syntax or tree-sitter artifact.

I6 NOT SATISFIED. No dedicated Quidra IDE and no Quidra IDE plugin was found in any editor marketplace or plugin repository, so no such artifact has a published release inside the 24 months before 2026-09-17.

I4 SATISFIED. Two independent routes: (i) 'Ruff' (charliermarsh.ruff, publisher Astral Software) in the Visual Studio Marketplace, admissible under clause (c) as the editor distribution of ruff, which python/cpython's CI invokes; (ii) 'Pylance' (ms-python.vscode-pylance, publisher Microsoft) and 'Python' (ms-python.python, publisher Microsoft) under the rubric-declared admission.

criteria_failed: I5 NOT SATISFIED. No member of Python's official_project_set publishes a TextMate grammar, a tree-sitter grammar or an editor major mode for Python. I2 SATISFIED. clangd's published feature page states 'Errors and warnings' (diagnostics), 'Code completion' and 'Find definition/declaration'.

cross_language_consistency_note: Every language was put through the identical six checks in the identical order, from the identical source types (E2 official documentation roots, E3 official repositories, E5 language-server/extension/grammar artefacts), and each check was resolved on a recorded verbatim excerpt rather than on knowledge of the language. Uniformity was enforced in four specific places. (1) Server selection: for every language the admissible servers were enumerated and the one covering the most of the six capabilities was selected, with the selection, its publisher, its clause and its feature-list URL recorded; ties were never reached. (2) Capability wording, rule R1: the same standard-of-statement was applied to all ten, and the same secondary search (other official doc pages, repository CHANGELOG, marketplace long description) was run wherever the primary list was incomplete -- it rescued Java's go-to-definition and did not rescue Swift's hover, and that asymmetry is a difference in the published evidence, not in the procedure. (3) I5, rule R2: every language's official organisation repository list and every first-party editor extension's grammar contributions were inspected the same way; this is why a grammar was found inside Oracle's Java extension and inside Kotlin's LSP repository, and why the absence of one in python/*, llvm-project, the golang organisation and quidra-lang is a verified negative rather than an unexamined gap. Under R2 three mature languages -- Python, C++ and Go -- fail I5 while Zig passes it, which is the correct observable result and was not adjusted. (4) Recency, I6: the same 24-month window ending 2026-09-17 and the same release-date field were used for all ten, and where the newest build post-dated the cutoff an earlier in-window release was cited instead. No language was credited for a capability that another language was denied on the same evidence, and no language was denied one that another was credited: the five languages at 100 (Rust, Java, TypeScript, Kotlin, Zig) each satisfy all six on positive evidence, the four at 80 (Python, C++, Go, Swift) each fail exactly one named indicator, and Quidra satisfies exactly one.
limitations: Java's I2/I3 and Python's I2/I3 (and one of Python's two routes to I4) rest on the frozen rubric's own declaration that the admissibility test admits jdt.ls and Pyright/Pylance. Independent clause (a), (b) or (c) evidence for those two tools was searched for and not found; the searches performed and the alternative scores (Java 60, Python 60) are recorded in admissibility_notes.

Swift's I3 turns on a documentation gap rather than on server behaviour: SourceKit-LSP is not stated by any first-party published feature list to provide hover, although find-references and rename are stated. Ten first-party documents were searched (listed in Swift's criteria_failed). No non-first-party source was substituted, and no behavioural test was run, because this metric's evidence_sources are E2/E3/E5 only and E1 execution is not admissible for it.

Java's I2/I3 go-to-definition evidence comes from the jdt.ls CHANGELOG rather than from the README feature bullets, whose relevant bullet is the umbrella term 'Code navigation'. The equivalent CHANGELOG search was run for every language whose primary feature list was incomplete.

I5 was resolved for Kotlin and for Java on grammars that those projects vendor from third-party sources (exoego/tree-sitter-kotlin; a snapshot of redhat-developer/vscode-java's java.tmLanguage.json) but publish and maintain in their own official repositories. Under the strict alternative reading -- that the grammar must have been authored inside the official_project_set -- Kotlin would fall to 80 and Java to 80. The reading actually applied (R2) is recorded, was fixed before Quidra was examined, and is the one the indicator's own wording supports.

Zig's I1 rests on clause (b) rather than clause (a): zls is published by zigtools, not by the Zig Software Foundation, and is admitted because ziglang.org names it. If clause (b) were removed Zig would lose I1, I2 and I3 and would score 40.

For C++ the MSVC-based integration named by the rubric was not investigated in depth, because clangd already satisfies I1, I2, I3, I4 and I6 under clause (a) and no ordering of servers could change C++'s count; the only C++ indicator in doubt, I5, cannot be satisfied by any Microsoft artefact since I5 is not widened by the admissibility test.

Per-language evidence records in the schema of global_rules.per_language_evidence_record (standard/rubrics/<metric_slug>/<language>.json), and the host_limited_indicators.json table, are not produced by this file; this metric uses only E2/E3/E5, so no indicator here was lost to a host-availability state S2, S3 or S4, and no entry is owed to that table from this metric.

Marketplace publisher and release-date fields were read from the Visual Studio Marketplace gallery API (extensionquery, filterType 7) and the JetBrains Marketplace API rather than from the rendered listing pages; the item URLs are recorded alongside so a reader can re-read the same fields from the pages.
